In this worksheet, payer type, payer share and the commercial-rate assumption change only the insurer and participant lines; the sponsor commitment does not fall because an insurer pays more for routine care. A line moves onto or off the sponsor only through its coverage status (who is billed), set by coverage review or a contract term, never through the insurer's payment amount. Payer and Medicare amounts can still inform the rate negotiated for research items (benchmark x sponsor_rate_multiplier).

assumptions.active_site_activation: Sunk activation for baseline-active sites is excluded equally from alternatives; activation for added sites is included.
assumptions.sponsor_administration: Sponsor administration is an operator input (for example study management, CRO and coordination costs). Scenario B applies the admin_reduction input to it as an assumption; no source of the reduction is modeled and no saving is claimed.
assumptions.contract_period: The budgeted contract period is an operator input: each selected site's monthly cost is multiplied by it. It is not a forecast of how long the trial runs.
assumptions.participant_split: Participants are split across selected sites in proportion to stated capacity (largest-remainder rounding, ties by site id). When C or E extends an existing network that lacks capacity, existing sites are filled to their stated capacity first and only the shortfall is split across added sites by capacity (plan.participant_split names the rule used). Capacity is an operator input.
assumptions.site_per_participant_cost: Site per-participant cost covers only site costs not itemized in the coverage worksheet (for example coordinator time and data entry); it must exclude every worksheet procedure, or that procedure is counted twice.
assumptions.access_support: Access support reimburses trial-related travel and lodging; it is not netted against, and does not pay, insurer cost sharing. Whether a sponsor may cover a beneficiary's cost sharing is a separate compliance question this worksheet does not model.
assumptions.feasibility: Feasible = stated capacity covers the target, sponsor commitment within budget, every selected site operator-flagged feasible, support at or above the floor. Actual site capabilities UNKNOWN.
assumptions.hospital_payment: Synthetic negotiated site costs for financial mechanics only; no claim of fair compensation or FMV.
assumptions.fee_benchmarks: Fee-schedule amounts are benchmarks. Research items the sponsor pays, and held contingency, are priced at benchmark x sponsor_rate_multiplier, an explicit stand-in for the rate negotiated with the site. Insurer and participant routine amounts use the benchmark, or are UNKNOWN for a commercial plan without the commercial-rate assumption.
assumptions.payer_benchmarks: Medicare and insurer amounts for routine care are benchmarks: they inform fair-market-value reasoning and are inputs to the sponsor's budget negotiation with each site or hospital.
assumptions.payer_billing: Whether an item may be billed to an insurer follows the protocol and coverage rules (for Medicare, NCD 310.1 routine costs in qualifying trials): research-only items are the sponsor's and are never billed to an insurer or participant. The site contract can still have the sponsor pay for a routine item (mark it SPONSOR here), and an item the sponsor pays for or supplies free is then not billed to the insurer. Insurer payment amounts are not a lever over who is billed.
assumptions.payer_independence: In this worksheet, payer type, payer share and the commercial-rate assumption change only the insurer and participant lines; the sponsor commitment does not fall because an insurer pays more for routine care. A line moves onto or off the sponsor only through its coverage status (who is billed), set by coverage review or a contract term, never through the insurer's payment amount. Payer and Medicare amounts can still inform the rate negotiated for research items (benchmark x sponsor_rate_multiplier).
assumptions.trial_target: Fixed demo target within every comparison, unrelated to the registered trial enrollment target.
assumptions.resource_costs: Separate synthetic 80% site/70% procedure cost assumptions, never inferred hospital margins.

limitations: Synthetic financial demonstration: all candidate sites, capacities, costs, margins and payer shares are hypothetical, not registered site facts or negotiated prices.
The real trial identifier links an existing illustrative authored schedule; the registry does not publish the complete protocol. This is not a sponsor-approved protocol budget.
Medicare and insurer amounts for routine care are benchmarks: they inform fair-market-value reasoning and are inputs to the sponsor's budget negotiation with each site or hospital.

Whether an item may be billed to an insurer follows the protocol and coverage rules (for Medicare, NCD 310.1 routine costs in qualifying trials): research-only items are the sponsor's and are never billed to an insurer or participant. The site contract can still have the sponsor pay for a routine item (mark it SPONSOR here), and an item the sponsor pays for or supplies free is then not billed to the insurer. Insurer payment amounts are not a lever over who is billed.

In this worksheet, payer type, payer share and the commercial-rate assumption change only the insurer and participant lines; the sponsor commitment does not fall because an insurer pays more for routine care. A line moves onto or off the sponsor only through its coverage status (who is billed), set by coverage review or a contract term, never through the insurer's payment amount. Payer and Medicare amounts can still inform the rate negotiated for research items (benchmark x sponsor_rate_multiplier).

Nothing here models negotiation length, enrollment speed, time to fill sites or trial duration, and no scenario is ranked or recommended; the budgeted contract period is an input that prices monthly site costs.
Routine coverage is potential, subject to qualifying-trial, beneficiary, jurisdiction, plan, network and service review. No insurer participates or commits funding.
Unknown responsibility is held as sponsor contingency, not billed to insurers or participants. Unresolved patient exposure is unknown, not evidence of zero liability.

Only the authored non-repeating visits (screening, cycles 1-8, end of treatment, safety follow-up) are priced. Actual drug acquisition/manufacturing, later treatment, complications and downstream outcomes are unknown; the drug contingency is an assumption, not a complete trial cost.

Access support reimburses trial-related travel and lodging; it is not netted against, and does not pay, insurer cost sharing. Whether a sponsor may cover a beneficiary's cost sharing is a separate compliance question this worksheet does not model.

Each worksheet line is assigned to one party (sponsor, insurer, participant or sponsor contingency). That is not a billing-compliance review and does not establish that no item is billed twice. Site per-participant costs must exclude every itemized worksheet procedure, or that procedure is counted twice.

Participants are split across selected sites in proportion to stated capacity, an operator input; when an existing network that lacks capacity is extended, existing sites are filled to their stated capacity first and only the shortfall goes to added sites. It is not a measured or predicted enrollment.
Sensitivity varies only site cost inputs (seeded lognormal spread); the ranges are not calibrated intervals.
Sponsor-to-hospital payments are transfers. Consolidated resource costs use separate explicit cost assumptions; a lower sponsor payment is not automatically a system or payer saving.
No claims, reimbursements, coverage authorizations, contracts or patient-identifiable records are transmitted. Operator corrections are interpretations, not clinical or payer attestations.
